issues.title: Phase1 S1→S3 common adapter — implemented but no longer on frozen critical path
issues.body:
## Resolution

The deterministic oracle-blind adapter now exists as:
`tools/build_s3_state_from_s1.py`
protocol `PHASE1_S1_TO_S3_STATE_ADAPTER_V1`.

It validates fixture identity and S1 hash, rejects oracle-bearing inputs, derives a deterministic S3 semantic state, records the source S1 hash, and emits canonical content hashes.

The original A/B path this issue blocked is no longer part of the frozen Phase1 critical path because TCC V2 terminates earlier at `EC_NATIVE_SCOPE_INCOMPATIBLE`.

Keep the adapter as reusable successor infrastructure; no further frozen-Phase1 work is required here. GitHub Actions remain disabled.

issues.title: Phase1 ECv4.4 M004 reframe divergence — preserved as research result
issues.body:
## Resolution

Actual ECv4.4 reframe result is canonical and must not be tuned away:
- aggregate reframe accuracy `9/10 = 0.90`
- M004 false-positive reframe: `REMOVE cause_x`, score `0.721 -> 0.848`
- M005 correct reframe: add authorization rejection variable, score `0.648 -> 0.846`

Canonical evidence:
`results/phase1_ecv44_reframe_actual_2026-10-03.json`

The 1.5B LLM follow-up also scored 0.90 but made the opposite discriminating error: M004 correct, M005 false-negative. This divergence is now incorporated into:
- `results/ec_llm_function_boundary_2026-10-03.json`
- `docs/EC_LLM_FUNCTION_BOUNDARY_2026-10-03.md`

No repair is authorized under the frozen Phase1 protocol. This issue is complete as an empirical finding. GitHub Actions remain disabled.

issues.title: Phase1 actual finding: EC next-action authority is singleton and not isomorphic to S3 admissible-set selection
issues.body:
## Actual interface verification on 2026-10-03

Pinned EC source:
- repo: `mokumaisancho/GPT-EC-Closure-Engine`
- commit: `d5ec423968f1c9242c590e5e77ccfd92d1f59eb2`
- native API: `v4.ec_next_action_authority.select_next_action`
- direct regression evidence: `01_repo/tests/test_ec_next_action_authority.py::test_ec_selects_exactly_one_next_action`

The EC-native control contract returns exactly one next action/work item.

The frozen Phase1 S3 contract instead returns `selected_candidate_ids[]` and explicitly requires multiple selected candidates in:
- M003: two COMPETING admissible routes must both remain selected/open.
- M009: two EQUIVALENT admissible actions must both remain selected.

## Finding
The two interfaces are not isomorphic.

This is **not** an EC accuracy failure. It is an architectural/contract result:
- EC native function: singular next-action authority.
- Phase1 S3 tested function: all-admissible-candidate-set selection plus reframing.

Eight of ten frozen fixtures require a singleton selected set; two require multi-selection. `8/10` is therefore only direct output-cardinality coverage, **not selection accuracy**.

## Required handling
1. Do not label a harness loop/filter as pure `EC_NATIVE` selection.
2. Under `PHASE1_EC_NATIVE_ADAPTER_V1`, mark full admissible-set selection as `EC_NATIVE_NOT_APPLICABLE` unless a versioned semantics-preserving outer iteration is explicitly introduced and attributed to `ADAPTER`.
3. Continue to report EC-native reframing independently; its actual Phase1-v2 result is already measured separately.
4. Treat native `next-action authority` as a distinct subfunction that EC can implement directly.
5. Any future adapter must preserve M003/M009 multiplicity and must not collapse them to one candidate.
6. GitHub Actions remain disabled.

Blocks Issue #23 from claiming full S3 selection as native ECv4.4.

issues.title: Phase1 actual finding: S4 closure is not identifiable from frozen S3 artifact
issues.body:
## Actual identifiability audit on 2026-10-03

The frozen Phase1 S3 artifact was audited as the declared upstream interface for S4.

Using only generic closure-relevant structural fields available in the frozen S3 contract:
- selected candidate count
- rejected candidate count
- `reframe_required`
- trigger residual types

there are collisions with different frozen closure labels.

### Collision A
Signature `(selected=1, rejected=1, reframe=false, residuals=[])`:
- CLOSE: M001, M002, M004, M006, M008, M010
- CONTINUE: M007

### Collision B
Signature `(selected=2, rejected=1, reframe=false, residuals=[])`:
- CONTINUE: M003
- CLOSE: M009

M005 is separately identifiable through its reframe/residual state.

## Quantified bound
A deterministic classifier using only these generic structural S3 fields can score at most `8/10 = 0.80` by majority choice within identical signatures.

This `0.80` is **not EC accuracy**. It is an interface-identifiability upper bound under the frozen S3 representation.

## Architectural interpretation
EC closure/run-state authority expects richer state than the current generic S3 artifact exposes. In particular, the current frozen interface does not generically expose enough information to distinguish at least:
- competing vs equivalent multi-selection (M003 vs M009),
- unresolved required condition vs otherwise closed singleton states (M007 vs several CLOSE fixtures).

Using operation-name/string special cases would turn the closure layer into a fixture/domain lookup and is not an acceptable generic EC authority.

## Required handling
1. Under `PHASE1_MVP_TCC_V1`, do not report an EC S4 closure accuracy from a simulated harness rule.
2. Mark native EC S4 as `NOT_IDENTIFIABLE_FROM_FROZEN_S3_INTERFACE` / `EC_NATIVE_NOT_APPLICABLE` for this protocol.
3. Preserve this as an experimental architecture/interface result, not an implementation bug.
4. Any future S3 enrichment (candidate relation, unresolved required conditions, residual/open-work/evidence state) requires a new versioned methodology/protocol; do not mutate the frozen run.
5. Oracle substitution at S4 remains possible only as an explicit intervention, not evidence that EC could infer the missing state.
6. GitHub Actions remain disabled.

Blocks Issue #23 from claiming reportable generic EC-native S4 closure under the current frozen interface.

issues.title: 1.5B capacity branch — resolved by valid 2CPU/8GB execution
issues.body:
## Resolution — actual 1.5B execution completed on 2026-10-03

The earlier Render-free 512MiB runtime failure was a host-resource blocker only. It did not represent a model/assay failure.

A later frozen follow-up ran the same assay on a valid 2 CPU / 8 GB execution path without changing fixtures, prompt, grammar, temperature, dataset digest, or model quantization.

Verified target:
- `bartowski/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct-GGUF`
- `Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf`
- size `986,048,768` bytes
- SHA-256 `1adf0b11065d8ad2e8123ea110d1ec956dab4ab038eab665614adba04b6c3370`
- dataset digest `8bfce027bdc82a34b78e9b1a87f7812d907db34c164f50a9a996bd41b3b824d6`

Actual result:
- 10/10 inference calls completed
- accuracy `9/10 = 0.90`
- predictions: NO=10, YES=0
- only M005 false negative
- 0.5B -> 1.5B improvement: `+0.80`
- frozen capacity-collapse condition resolved
- no automatic 4B branch permitted

Canonical evidence:
`results/phase1_qwen25_1p5b_reframe_actual_2026-10-03.json`

Research consequence:
The 0.5B collapse was capacity-dependent. At 1.5B, LLM and EC both score 0.90 on the fixed reframe assay, but disagree on M004/M005, so aggregate equality does not imply functional equivalence.

Google Drive model relay and GitHub Actions were not used.
